articles.title: I’m Rolling My Eyes At Claims That Ezra Frech Losing His Prosthetic Won Him Dancing With The Stars
articles.summary: I can't imagine why anyone would think this.
articles.content:
Dancing with the Stars ' Season 35 finale just aired on the 2026 TV schedule , and congratulations are in order for Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. While there's no shortage of fans who are happy for the duo, there are a few disgruntled people who feel his win over Amber Glenn and others came because he lost his prosthetic during his final dance. It's a wild take that's making rounds, and I can't help but roll my eyes at it.

The moment received raucous applause from the in-house audience, and the judges awarded him perfect scores. Unfortunately, comments like the one below have since been floating around X , with some arguing Frech received sympathy votes and calling fans ableist for not penalizing him for the incident:

I can't help but take a deep sigh when reading this take, and admittedly, I'm not the only one who has taken issue this person. With that said, if there are more people out there who quietly believe or think that Ezra's disability is what pushed him across the finish line to be the latest person to win Dancing with the Stars , let me just point out a couple of details.

To chalk Ezra Frech's win up to his final dance of the season discredits a run that was one of the best we've seen this entire season. He was never at the bottom of the leaderboard and was even at the top for a few weeks. Frech never had an off week, not once, which is the type of resilience we expect from Olympic athletes.

If Ezra Frech gained additional votes in Dancing with the Stars ' finale after his freestyle performance, it wasn't out of sympathy. That would imply the dance fell to disaster after he lost his prosthetic, and that simply wasn't the case. Frech not only finished the dance, he completed the routine hardly missing a beat.

Had Connor Wood, Maura Higgins, Amber Glenn, or Tatyana Ali recovered from a disastrous moment with such poise, I feel confident the judges and audience would've reacted the same way. This is especially true on DWTS ' finale night, in which I feel the judges want their scores to impact the end result as little as possible.

articles.title: The Hunger Games Team Reveals the Biggest Mistake the Franchise Made, And They're Right
articles.summary: The Hunger Games has made a name for itself as an incredibly popular franchise for nearly 20 years, but it's true that they made this one mistake. The Hunger Games is once again making headlines following the debut of the latest (and perhaps final) installment, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. This new movie, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Hunger Games has made a name for itself as an incredibly popular franchise for nearly 20 years, but it's true that they made this one mistake. The Hunger Games is once again making headlines following the debut of the latest (and perhaps final) installment, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping . This new movie, which hit theaters just last week, focuses on Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark's mentor, Haymitch Abernathy, during his own Hunger Games and is therefore a prequel. However, the movie concludes with a scene involving Katniss and Peeta , so attention has understandably returned to those characters and their movies as well.

Those movies represent the original trilogy of Hunger Games books ; however, they were turned into four movies, with the last book, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay , being split into two parts. This was far from unheard of at the time. The Harry Potter movies, for example, had the same approach with the final installment in that series, Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows , which was split into two movies. Yet, in reflecting on the franchise as a whole, Hunger Games producer Nina Jacobson revealed that her approach would be different now, were she to be making this decision again. Check out her comments below.

The decision to split Mockingjay into two movies likely had myriad justifications at the time, from the financial benefits of being able to profit off of two blockbuster movies rather than just one to the doubled run time allowing for a greater exploration of the book's plot. However, in looking back, Jacobson shared that she would not have the same mentality about it now. Speaking with Empire Magazine , she said, "Even though I love the Mockingjay films, if I had it to do over again, I think both Francis [Lawrence, director] and I might try to do it all in one… Mockingjay was such a big book, and it takes you to so many different places."

Jacobson continued, "But in the end, I think that Francis and I both felt that splitting them up…even if it did come from an inside-out place of really feeling like we needed two films to tell the story, I think audiences find it cynical. Even if its intentions are earnest, which they were. They feel like it's a play to make them see two films instead of one." This is an interesting perspective, and it's undoubtedly a true one. Fans were frustrated by this decision at the time, not only because it seemed to some like a grab for more money but also because it meant waiting even longer for the epic conclusion. And, as much as Jacobson's words are likely true, and they did have earnest intentions, the fact is that it did, in the end, mean more money for the studio.

Unfortunately, that backfired beyond just audiences being frustrated with the financial component, as Mockingjay - Part 1 and Mockingjay - Part 2 are the lowest-ranked movies of the original four. Both films come in at 70% on Rotten Tomatoes, whereas The Hunger Games is rated 85%, and The Hunger Games: Catching Fire is rated 90%. (Notably, though, both Sunrise on the Reaping and The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes come in under both Mockingjay films.) It's impossible to really say what would have been better; perhaps audiences would have complained about one movie feeling rushed or what it would have cut. Yet, Jacobson makes a great point, and this does seem like a franchise mistake.

Would you have preferred to see Mockingjay as just one movie, or did you like it being split into two? Share your thoughts in the comments down below.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence's 'Sex Swing' Comment When She Met Woody Harrelson Is The Most JLaw Comment Ever
articles.summary: There's making a first impression, and then there's the Jennifer Lawrence way.
articles.content:
Jennifer Lawrence has never struck me as someone who spends much time worrying about whether the next thing out of her mouth is appropriate. That's part of why her interviews are so entertaining. With The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping now part of the 2026 movie schedule , one of her earliest exchanges with Woody Harrelson is getting another airing. The story involves a bus, an unusual piece of equipment and one question I'm guessing he wasn't expecting from his new co-star.

Well, there it is. Most of us would probably get through saying our names before asking a new colleague about the mysterious swing hanging inside his bus. Lawrence apparently took one look at it and decided that question couldn't wait. Honestly, the fact that she managed any part of the introduction before asking might be the most surprising detail.

What's funny is that this isn't the first time Harrelson has shared the anecdote. The encounter made its way into a Rolling Stone profile around the release of the original Hunger Games in 2012 . Hearing him tell it to Zada all these years later is especially amusing because he still seems to get such a kick out of remembering it.

During their conversation, Harrelson also reflected on how much he enjoyed the original cast. "My God, did we have fun," he recalled. "It was such a good group." He fondly remembered Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Liam Hemsworth , along with the lively atmosphere they created behind the scenes. Given the story about that first meeting, it seems about right. I can't imagine the Silver Linings Playbook star was responsible for a particularly quiet set.

2013's The Hunger Games: Catching Fire owned the previous best Tuesday for the franchise with $15.96M. Running cume for the fifth Francis Lawrence movie is $148.1M and by Thanksgiving at least Sunrise on the Reaping will surpass its previous 2023 chapter's lifetime domestic B.O. of $166.3M.

We're still waiting on Disney's official number for its previews on Walt Disney Animation's Hexed , but last night we were spotting $2M which is higher than Encanto ($1.5M previews, 5-day of $40.5M) and Wish ($1.8M previews including $500K Saturday sneaks; 5-day of $31.6M). No RT audience score yet, but critics were meh at 67% fresh.

articles.title: 'Clashing Through the Snow' Director Carlson Young on Going From "Horror Girly" to Holiday Rom-Com
articles.summary: The director and former 'Scream' star talks about finding the "psychic predator" in a holiday road-trip romance, filming with her daughter and telling more romance stories — while staying ready to bring her "horror fangs out."
articles.content:
Near the end of Clashing Through the Snow , Michelle Randolph 's Hannah Hendricks walks past an Eloise portrait in a New York hotel lobby. Standing beside it, holding her then seven-month-old daughter, is the film's director, Carlson Young .

"It really choked me up, even as I was walking through the shot," Young tells The Hollywood Reporter.

The moment felt "spiritually correct" for the rising director, who recalls dressing as Kay Thompson's Eloise for her fourth-grade book day. Filming it with her baby on her hip gave her "this kind of out-of-body experience, overlapping-reality thing" that she felt "a lot of little girls could relate to." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV How Amin Joseph Brought "Humanity" to Sonny Liston in 'The Greatest' TV How 'Landman' Star Michelle Randolph Found Love ... In a Rental Car

It's a heartwarming moment in a heartwarming movie, and perhaps a surprising film for a director who calls herself a "horror girly."

Before moving behind the camera, Young built her career as an actor, with credits including Key & Peele , a guest role on Netflix's Emily in Paris and the 2014 comedy Premature . Her breakout came as Brooke Maddox on MTV's Scream , the 2015 TV series adaptation of the horror film franchise created by Kevin Williamson and directed by Wes Craven, and Young credits the horror genre with making her want to tell stories in the first place.

"When I was a little girl, horror got me out of bed in the morning. Those are the directors I watched as a kid that made me want to be a director and a storyteller."

Having worked with "incredible horror directors on Scream ," Young became fascinated by "what fear has to teach us," and that curiosity guides her work as a director, even in romance. Her horror "sensibility and natural instinct," she says, allow her to "clearly identify, in any given scene, where the psychic predator actually is." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Years later, Young has directed Prime Video 's new cozy holiday rom-com, with snowstorms, rental cars, a bus full of elderly passenger, bookstores and enemies-to-lovers banter, and she says those horror instincts and her love for nostalgic romances are exactly what helped her find its heart.

"I didn't necessarily think my next movie would be a holiday rom-com, but I fell in love with the script," she tells THR . "It reminded me of so many classic holiday rom-coms that I'm nostalgic for."

Clashing Through the Snow , which debuted on Prime Video on Monday, stars Landman' s Michelle Randolph and The Summer I Turned Pretty breakout Chris Briney as Hannah Hendricks and Ryan Mitchell, rival book editors competing for a career-saving publishing deal. When their flight is canceled, the pair are forced to share a rental car to New York City in the middle of a holiday snowstorm, each determined to close the deal first. And of course chaos ensues with the holiday journey anything but jolly.

The film, which can also serve as a love letter to books and reading, was pitched as a Planes, Trains and Automobiles for a new generation, a comparison Young says she had to shed "right off the bat" or risk being overwhelmed by anxiety. Still, she found her film's driving force in the heart of the 1987 road-trip comedy: the moment John Candy's Del Griffith tells Steve Martin's Neal Page, "I like me." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In Clashing Through the Snow , that heart comes in a vulnerable motel-room conversation in which Ryan tells Hannah she's "living a when-then life." The line spoke personally to Young and became the foundation for the film's long, funny and often chaotic journey.

"It resonated with me deeply, and I felt like it's in the zeitgeist. So yes, it's a comedy of errors, hijinks ensue, it's a very fun movie, but it does have something to say as well," Young says. "I did try to do our own version — pay homage to the classic holiday movies that we come back to every year and try to do something new."

Clashing Through the Snow may be her newest film, but it also marks a milestone for the director, who kept a "when-then" promise of her own.

"I told myself, 'When I direct three movies, then I can have a baby.' And that's actually what happened," she says. "It's really cool to bring my daughter into a world where I'm able to do what I'm passionate about and have her by my side. What could be more beautiful than that?"

Young was on the sunny beaches of Mallorca, Spain, wrapping production on Prime Video's romantic drama The Last Sunrise when she set her sights on Clashing . She would trade a sun-soaked summer romance for a snowy, cross-country road trip that takes place during the holiday season. And though she was already attached to direct, she still needed the right home for it.

She had already worked with Amazon on the 2024 romance Upgraded , starring Camila Mendes, and on The Last Sunrise , with Maia Reffico, Fernando Lindez and Eva Longoria, which was then still forthcoming (it debuted in July 2026). For Clashing , her third film with Amazon, she again found a partner in the streamer. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It made sense, and it's a movie I really believed in and knew would be great there with the team at Amazon," Young says of bringing the film to Prime Video.

With two films out on Prime Video this year, Young has come a long way from her directorial debut, the short film The Blazing World , which premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival. Since then she has directed the 2021 feature-length version of The Blazing World ; Upgraded , which has a confirmed sequel; and the survival thriller Trust , starring Sophie Turner.

And while her turn as fan favorite Brooke Maddox in MTV's iteration of the iconic horror franchise catered to her love for horror, Clashing and its exploration of "living a when-then life" made for a personal, art-imitating-life moment for the director.

"I catch myself in that pattern almost constantly — this natural withholding of, 'I have to accomplish this before I can give myself this.' I think that's very reflective of the world we live in, with the overstimulation and the high speed. We live in overdrive, so it's something I deal with in real time," she says.

"From a career perspective, I hope to be able to look back at the end of my life and feel meaning in the work I've done. I try really hard with every movie I direct to weave in the medicine I'm capable of reflecting at the time."

With The Last Sunrise and now Clashing Through the Snow, the films have marked breakout moments for their leading stars. The Last Sunrise marked Lindez's first English-language role, while Clashing is Randolph and Briney's first foray as leading rom-com stars. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Having come up as an actor first, Young has found a kinship in directing talent amid these moments in their journey.

"I understand how vulnerable it is to be an actor. I think that's a really important thing for directors to be sensitive to — and to know that actors also have incredible ideas. So I love to let whoever I'm working with play, and having been an actress first informs so much of what I do."

And how does acting inform her directing? She approaches it from a "different altitude."

"I don't read a script anymore and think, 'Oh wow, I'd really like to play this character.' I read a script now with this bird's-eye view. I feel much more spider-like, weaving different stories and characters together. But I'm actor-first, character-first, so it informs every decision I make as a director."

Briney is a talent she predicts "has a long career ahead of him, with many places to go and explore."

"I felt like seeing him in a more comedic role would be something incredibly fresh for him. When I met him and spoke to him, it was very obvious that he could do that, so I was really excited to find this character with him. He's a very charming human, and he's kind and resourceful. We got to have a lot of fun on set — I would just pitch him jokes and he would land them. He has a real comedic flexibility that I think is super fresh in his generation of actors," she says.

As for Randolph, Young was struck by the "charm and warmth that she exudes." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"She just has this effortless charm of the '90s and 2000s rom-coms that I think we're all so nostalgic for."

Young says of pairing them, "They're both incredibly charming and talented actors in their own right, so it's a dream to put those two together."

In addition to Briney and Randolph, the film features a host of familiar faces, including Julia Fox, Andrew Schulz, Lucas Gage, Jake Shane, Tan France, Zarna Garg and even Paris Hilton. Young laughs when it's suggested the internet showed up for the road trip.

"You took the words right out of my mouth. The internet is showing up for this road trip," she says. "This movie is for the chronically online."

Each brought the kind of levity the story needed, she says, and the known faces give the audience a familiarity "that feels like a warm hug. You kind of know this person; you're aware of the energy they bring. It was a really fun recipe. It's like a cake of the internet."

As for Hilton, who shares a comedic exchange with Briney's Ryan at one point in the film, Young explains that the randomness of her guest role made the rivalry between Ryan and Hannah even more fun. "We were like, who is a person Ryan could interface with at the Bianca Hart show who would make Hannah go, 'How the fuck do you — what is going on here?' She's so iconic in her own right, and picturing her in that moment made me laugh out loud."

"I want to do many more rom-coms. I want to do a lot more romance. "So far in my career I've sailed across different genres, and I'm extremely motivated by asking myself, 'Why do people like this genre?' That motivates me to go try to fall in love with it. I'm just trying to understand love, and it takes a trillion forms. We're specks in the universe in a nanosecond of geological time. There's a simplicity I like — like a good poem that has to iterate itself over and over again to get to a truly beautiful form."

Clashing arrives as onscreen love stories are booming and having now made several of her own, Young believes that "in this digital age we live in, human connection and the intimacy of human relationships are actually kind of novel at this point.

She adds, "As women, we escape into romanticism because there are men and women out there who are able to see you, proverbially, and connect with you at a very deep level — and I think that's sometimes quite hard to find in the real world. Going forward, Young also finds great inspiration in "female characters who have a journey to go on."

articles.title: 'Hunger Games' Producer Admits 'Mockingjay' Should Have Been One Movie
articles.summary: Franchise producer Nina Jacobson says adapting one book into two movies rubs fans the wrong way: "I think audiences find it cynical."
articles.content:
The first two Hunger Games movies? Terrific. Critics and fans agree.

The next two Hunger Games movies? Well…

Author Suzanne Collins' climactic Katniss novel Mockingjay was infamously split into two films, Part 1 and Part 2 . Both are considered a step down from the previous two Hunger Games blockbusters, with lower Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores. The uneven Part 1 , in particular, felt like a franchise spinning its wheels. To fans, it all looked like a studio trying to wring more ticket sales from the story. Related Stories Movies Jennifer Lawrence Thinks Her 'Hunger Games' Bow and Arrow Prop Was Stolen Movies 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Review: A Worthier Prequel to the Dystopian Battle Royale, Powered by Joseph Zada's Star-Making Turn

In a new interview with Empire , franchise producer Nina Jacobson says that if she and director Francis Lawrence had a second chance, they'd adapt Mockingjay into a single movie. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Even though I love the Mockingjay films, if I had it to do over again, I think both Francis and I might try to do it all in one," Jacobson said. " Mockingjay was such a big book, and it takes you to so many different places. But in the end, I think that Francis and I both felt that splitting them up… even if it did come from an inside-out place of really feeling like we needed two films to tell the story, I think audiences find it cynical. Even if its intentions are earnest, which they were. They feel like it's a play to make them see two films instead of one."

The producer added: "We really put the burden on ourselves [now], even when it's a big book, to transform it into a theatrical experience, to not take advantage of your audience’s patience, to make it as tight as we can. [ Sunrise On The Reaping ] is the longest [film] by a minute or two of all of them." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At the time, splitting the final book in a fantasy franchise into two films was a bit of a trend. Warner Bros. did it with JK Rowling's Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows and Summit did it with Stephenie Meyer's' Breaking Dawn .

And while the Mockingjay films were considered creatively weaker than the previous two movies, they still were generally liked — neither was an outright misstep — and did boffo box office, with 2014's Part 1 grossing $775 million and 2015's Part 2 grossing $653 million.

The new film, Sunrise on the Reaping , grossed a strong $120 million in its opening weekend, marking a rebound for the franchise after the soft launch of 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6 million).

articles.summary: In theory, box office and awards shouldn't have any correlation, but in practice, the higher profile movies often do better; regardless, Supergirl just got shortlisted for the Best Visual Effects Oscar, which even most of its critics might admit it has a shot at. After all, another widely disliked DC movie, Suicide Squad, actually won […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In theory, box office and awards shouldn't have any correlation, but in practice, the higher profile movies often do better; regardless, Supergirl just got shortlisted for the Best Visual Effects Oscar, which even most of its critics might admit it has a shot at. After all, another widely disliked DC movie, Suicide Squad , actually won an Oscar for Best Hair and Make-up . There are 20 movies in all on the shortlist, as reported in Variety ; some, like the live-action Moana remake, are even less popular than Supergirl . Most have fantasy or sci-fi elements, with The Mosquito Bowl and Heart of the Beast standing out as more realistic.

Supergirl is set almost entirely in outer space, on alien worlds and a floating space city. It features a main character who can convincingly fly and shoot heat vision, and her lovable pet dog who isn't actually there on set. Thought the main villain, Krem of the Yellow Hills, is just a tall, pierced guy in armor, the rest of the story is full of aliens, including one that defecates snack food. (Where's that souvenir popcorn bucket?)

The frontrunners for the award are probably Godzilla Minus Zero , since its predecessor won; Project Hail Mary , which boasted that its special effects were mainly practical , and featured a puppet co-lead; Dune: Part Three , which closes out a beloved trilogy that was begun by a multi Oscar-winner ; and possibly Wildwood , if the voters decide that animation can be its own special effect. Marvel superhero movies in contention include Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday ; Star Wars has The Mandalorian and Grogu . On the cheaper end of the spectrum, the infinite seeming locations of Backrooms have Kane Parsons' breakthrough feature in contention.

Notably not in contention is Masters of the Universe , which Amazon-MGM declined to submit for awards consideration, though their other Nicholas Galitzine-starring movie, The Sheep Detectives , is shortlisted. Presumably they want Project Hail Mary to be the big sci-fi epic they put their might behind; we can probably expect Warner Bros. to likewise focus on Dune rather than Supergirl , but they at least gave both a shot. The Hindu religious epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend , domestically distributed by Sony, made the shortlist, as, inevitably, did The Odyssey . Dystopias are represented by Digger and The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , while Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day mixed reality and aliens.

Rounding up the top twenty is Whalefall , which convincingly simulated the inside of a whale's stomach. Most, if not all of us, will never know firsthand how accurate its re-creation is or is not, but it certainly beats the live-action Pinocchio movie from Disney+ that came out a couple years ago. Supergirl isn't likely to win, or even make the final five — as a space movie, Project Hail Mary is more of a fave; as a superhero movie, Spider-Man is way more popular. Still, given the negativity the movie faced — so much so that David Krumholtz decided to take a pause from acting — even this consideration is a win.

Are you happy to see Supergirl get some respect from the Academy? Fly into comments below with your thoughts.

articles.title: Doomsday Artist Shares Multiverse-Crossing Yelena Moment That Would Have Been Amazing
articles.summary: New Avengers: Doomsday concept art reveals a surprising upgrade for Florence Pugh's Yelena, and it has a Spider-Man twist. Even before Marvel's next big event hyped fans with new trailers and footage, there were pretty high expectations for how it would work as a crossover. Not only will the film bring the MCU's Earth with […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google New Avengers: Doomsday concept art reveals a surprising upgrade for Florence Pugh's Yelena , and it has a Spider-Man twist. Even before Marvel's next big event hyped fans with new trailers and footage , there were pretty high expectations for how it would work as a crossover. Not only will the film bring the MCU's Earth with the alternate world seen in The Fantastic Four: First Steps , but the Fox X-Men will also collide , bringing at least three different realities together. An early storyboard for Doomsday hints at another one, though.

Storyboard artist Phil Langone, whose Marvel credits include the first three Spider-Man movies, WandaVision , Thunderbolts , and, yes, Avengers: Doomsday , took to social media to share the art. In the image, Yelena is traversing a mysterious terrain with a caption that says "A spirit swirls behind Yelena," but it's not the background that has caught fans' attention; it's what she's riding. In the image, it appears the MCU's new Black Widow is on top of the Green Goblin's Goblin Glider, and it looks a lot like the one from Willem Dafoe's version of the character .

View this post on Instagram Avengers: Doomsday Concept Art Teases an Unannounced Spider-Man Villain It's worth noting that if this moment was actually something that happened in the film, it's very likely that Marvel would have already put the kibosh on it being shared publicly. That said, even Langone himself isn't sure if it's actually in the film, as he captioned the image: "Just a little storyboard panel among many. Take from this drawing what you will… I have no idea what this movie will be like or it’s story as this was done almost two years ago."

As Marvel fans may recall, concept art leaked over a year ago that showed off a slew of characters that aren't even confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday. It's possible that the art that Langone shared was part of that initial batch, or that this art was for Avengers: Secret Wars . In any event, Marvel clearly developed a slew of ideas for Doomsday that would have remixed the crossover aspect of the film to a surprising degree.

Even if this moment isn't part of Avengers: Doomsday , it begs the question: Why would Yelena have the Green Goblin's glider at all? The design for the vehicle is unmistakable too, and almost makes it seem like the world from Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man may have had a bigger part to play in the film in earlier drafts ( rumors persist that the universe from Sam Raimi's films will still be seen in some form ).

One thing is for sure, though: Marvel has made it clear that Pugh's character, even though she doesn't have superpowers, is one of the new foundations that the MCU is built on. Not only was last summer's Thunderbolts largely built around her own emotional journey, but her cameo appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day further solidified it. In the long history of "no-brainers" that the MCU has focused on, making an Oscar-nominated star that appeals to young audiences around the globe may be at the top of the list.

articles.title: Path of Exile 2's Critical Strike Changes Are Great, But Its Biggest Itemization Problem Remains
articles.summary: Courtesy of Grinding Gear Games There are few things more satisfying in an ARPG than watching a build finally come together. You spend hours chasing the right equipment and tweaking your passive tree until every little interaction starts working, squeaky clean, in your favor. Then you find that one upgrade and suddenly your character feels like an entirely different beast. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are few things more satisfying in an ARPG than watching a build finally come together. You spend hours chasing the right equipment and tweaking your passive tree until every little interaction starts working, squeaky clean, in your favor. Then you find that one upgrade and suddenly your character feels like an entirely different beast. That's the magic of Path of Exile 2 . The best builds are product of experimentation and the obsessive pursuit of making an idea work. That's why I'm glad to see Grinding Gear Games rethink how critical strike chance works in its upcoming 1.0 release . Removing it from the passive tree is a change that could make all future progression more interesting.

Still, GGG is fixing one problem while leaving an arguably bigger one sitting right in the middle of its itemization. Critical strike chance had become so easy to stack that investing in felt more like an obligation. The same kind of pressure exists with +Level modifiers on equipment. These modifiers can provide such an enormous boost to a skill effectiveness that weapons without them often struggle to compete, even when its other properties should make it an exciting alternative. Truthfully, GGG should absolutely abolish +Level modifiers from gear entirely.

Let's be honest. Critical strikes are one of the most appealing ways to build a damage-focused character. There's a thrill in watching an attack connect, and destroy anything it touched. The trouble is that critical strike chance had become so accessible in Path of Exile 2 that reaching 100% really felt like the beginning of a build, rather the culmination of a carefully assembled character. More like another box to tick. Once a build could reliably guarantee critical hits, the decision to invest in crit became considerably less interesting. There wasn't really a meaningful trade-off. You were just following the path toward the damage ceiling.

That's why I wholeheartedly agree with GGG's decision to remove critical strike chance from the passive tree. Moving that responsibility toward equipment gives weapons a much more meaningful role in determining how a character deals damage. A player who wants to build around critical strikes now has to think more carefully about the gear they're chasing. Meanwhile, the passive tree can focus on making those critical hits more devastating rather than helping players reach a threshold that was becoming increasingly routine. I love that distinction. It creates a more interesting relationship between a character's equipment and their progression, which is exactly the sort of decision-making that makes an ARPG worth sinking hundreds of hours into. There is still plenty of room for crit-focused builds to be spectacular. Getting there should simply require a little more thought.on.

Now, let's talk about the elephant: +Level modifiers. Most PoE 2 players know that +Level modifiers are incredibly powerful because they improve the skills that define a build in the first place. A weapon with several additional levels to the skills you're using can provide such a substantial increase in effectiveness that its other properties become totally secondary. This creates an awkward situation where players aren't necessarily looking for the most interesting weapon for their build. Instead, they're looking for the weapon that gives their abilities the biggest numerical advantage. I mean, that's a given, sure. But, even when another piece of equipment offers a genuinely exciting combination of effects, it can be difficult to justify using it when those extra skill levels are sitting on the other side of the comparison.

Unique weapons are where I think this problem becomes especially frustrating. These items are supposed to offer something special. Their identity should come from the unusual mechanics they introduce or the way they encourage players to approach a build differently. Finding a unique that completely changes how an ability functions should be an exciting moment. Yet when its power has to compete against the sheer effectiveness of additional skill levels, that excitement can disappear rather quickly. Why would I want to build around an interesting weapon if a rare alternative with +Levels gives my skills a substantially better foundation?

A unique shouldn't automatically be the best item in every situation, of course. But it should have a meaningful opportunity to compete without being immediately dismissed because it lacks one overwhelmingly valuable modifier. There are some builds that do without the +Levels, but… really, its a trade-off that's not at all fair right now. Some of the most creative equipment in the game becomes little more than a collection of interesting ideas players admire before putting it back in their stash.

Again, GGG should remove +Level modifiers from equipment, especially weapons. Yes, that would require a substantial rethink of how skill progression works and how players acquire power throughout the game. I'm not pretending it's a small adjustment. But I'd rather see developers tackle that challenge than continue balancing around a modifier that can overshadow so much of what makes itemization exciting.

Skills should grow through the character's progression while equipment gives players more interesting ways to shape skill functionality. Imagine finding a unique weapon that inspires an entirely new build because of its mechanics rather than feeling compelled to compare its skill levels against another drop. Path of Exile 2 can make equipment feel more genuinely transformative, and I would love to see GGG push that philosophy even further. The critical strike changes are a fantastic start. Now let's give every other item a reason to be exciting, too.

Do you think +Level modifiers have become too important in Path of Exile 2 , or should GGG preserve them as a major part of gearing? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comment section below.

articles.title: Thor's First Appearance Comic Is Still Valued At Over $3,000 Despite Being In The Worst Possible Condition
articles.summary: There are many things that determine an item's value at an auction, but it's the item itself that primarily sets the bar. Rare vintage items like comics and toys have seen their valuation skyrocket over the past few years. Then there's the grade; items with higher grades tend to be more valuable than those with […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are many things that determine an item's value at an auction, but it's the item itself that primarily sets the bar. Rare vintage items like comics and toys have seen their valuation skyrocket over the past few years. Then there's the grade; items with higher grades tend to be more valuable than those with a lower one or no grade at all. However, the former condition always trumps the latter, as demonstrated by this issue of Journey Into Mystery #83 , in which Thor made his first appearance. Despite getting the lowest possible grade of CGC FR 1.0 and having cream to off-white pages, the issue recently sold for $3,050 at Heritage Auctions.

Like many of The Avengers, Thor's popularity shot up after the advent of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. While we all recognize the Asgardian God thanks the Chris Hemsworth, he wasn't always the son of Odin we know him as today. In fact, his origin was quite different in his first appearance. Dr. Donald Blake just happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time when aliens from Saturn invaded. Finding himself trapped in a cave, Blake came upon a stick which he tried to use to escape the cave. Upon tapping the stick, he found out that it was actually Mjolnir in disguise, and was himself transformed into Thor. The newly empowered hero thwarted the alien attack and transformed back into Donald Blake before anyone noticed. This humble origin story is a far cry from the prince of Asgard we know today, and is perhaps why the issue is so valuable despite its condition.

Dr. Donald Blake and this origin story were eventually retconned by Marvel, making Thor the Odinson we know him as today. He did reemerge to make a few appearances over the years, though, eventually becoming a villain. However, since the Asgardian version has become so popular now, this first appearance comic has seen its value soar to such an extent that even the low grade couldn't stop it from getting a valuation of above $3,000. First-appearance comics do tend to sell for way more than that, especially if it involves one of the most popular superheroes in recent years, but managing to get this amount despite the grade, and a whole laundry list of physical defects is a feat worthy of a God.

Younger fans will find it hard to believe that Thor wasn't originally born in the golden halls of Valaskjalf in Asgard, but was just a guy who found a magical stick one day. It's facts like this that make the comic book industry's long history so fascinating and worth preserving. Perhaps that's why the new owner of this Journey Into Mystery #83 paid such a high price despite its condition. If it weren't for collectors like themselves, perhaps everyone would have forgotten about Thor's original backstory and Dr. Donald Blake would be lost among the branches of Yggdrasil. It's good to know that even in this terrible state, the issue is still worth so much to fans and collectors.

Do you prefer Thor's original backstory or his Asgardian one? Let us know in the comments.

With 2027 fast approaching, it's time to look ahead to all of the new Shonen Jump franchise releases we'll see in the new year. […]

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Another major series from Shueisha's Shonen Jump library is making its official anime debut next year, and has dropped the first look at what to expect with its first full trailer. With 2027 fast approaching, it's time to look ahead to all of the new Shonen Jump franchise releases we'll see in the new year . This includes the titles from the digital Shonen Jump+ app, and Yu Chiba's Kindergarten Wars has been one of the most promising yet. Now even more fans are going to get to see why.

Kindergarten Wars is a fun spy action series that sees dangerous assassins tasked with protecting children at a daycare, but they must keep it hidden from all of them at all times. It's got the kind of look that makes it seem perfectly fitting for an anime adaptation , and now that's even more true now seeing it in motion with a new trailer confirming an April 2027 launch for the new series. You can check out the trailer and poster for Kindergarten Wars below.

Kindergarten Wars will be making its debut sometime next April as part of the Spring 2027 anime schedule , but no concrete release date or international release plans have been announced as of this time. Shinsuke Gomi will be directing the new anime for Sunrise and Felix Film with Junko Yamanaka providing the character designs, Takaomi Kanasaki providing the scripts, and Hiroshi Nakamura, Kenta Higashiohji, and Dai Haraguchi will be composing the music with Bandai Namco Filmworks overseeing the production.

Kindergarten Wars also confirms a voice cast including the likes of Atsumi Tanezaki as Rita, Kentaro Kumagai as Doug, Hitomi Ohwada as Hana, Satoshi Hino as Luke, Mariya Ise as Silvia, Romi Park as Erina, Tetsu Inada as Gordon, Mirei Kumagai as Mac, and Sumire Morohoshi as Una all revealed so far. It's also been revealed that Ado will be performing the opening theme for the series titled "Bibayatarametta," which can be heard in this new trailer as well.

Kindergarten Wars has been a stand out hit for Shonen Jump+ ever since it made its debut in 2022, and the series has been working through the final arc of the series with its latest chapters. Series creator Yu Chiba officially confirmed that to be the case last year, but it's yet to be revealed just how many more chapters are left given that the release schedule for the manga has been more relaxed through the past year as well. Either way, this new anime is about to introduce a lot more fans to the fold.

Kindergarten Wars has a blend of cute character art and designs with fun action, and that makes for a very interesting experience. Not only is it elevated with humor as a result of those designs, but the action takes a lot of fans by surprise too. If the anime can tap into that same balance of energy that the manga is able to dance around, it's going to be a fun time. But how are you feeling about the Kindergarten Wars anime so far? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus Made A Notable Choice With Her Wedding Where Billy Ray Cyrus Was Involved
articles.summary: It was an unconventional (but sweet) decision.
articles.content:
This past weekend was massive for Miley Cyrus , as the fan-favorite pop singer officially tied the knot with longtime partner Maxx Morando. Cyrus and Morando got married in Palm Springs on Saturday, November 21, where their friends and family were present. Among the attendees was Miley’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, from whom she was previously estranged . By all accounts, everyone seemed to have an enjoyable time during the ceremony though, interestingly, Miley made a significant choice as far as her dad was concerned.

Cyrus’ decision to have her mom walk her down the aisle is definitely big, but it also seems to speak volumes about the depths of their relationship. The mother-daughter duo have also seemed quite close, so it does track that Miley would bestow such an honor upon her mother. However, from the outside looking in, Billy Ray doesn’t seem torn up about not having taken that sacred stroll with his little girl. The “Achy Breaky Heart” singer took to his own Instagram to share some sweet thoughts about Miley’s wedding on her birthday:

Billy Ray Cyrus’ mere presence at the wedding represents a major milestone, given the former family drama he and Miley were entangled in. The father and daughter reportedly experienced a rift in their relationship after Billy Ray and Tish’s 2022 divorce . Also, in early 2025, Billy Ray and son Trace – whom he adopted after marrying Tish – were apparently on the outs, based on a candid letter Trace shared on social media. While Miley didn’t open up publicly about the situation, insiders claimed she was looking to distance herself from the family drama . Throughout the estrangement, Billy Ray also paid tribute to Miley and, while it allegedly took some time, the two mended fences.

articles.title: The Ultimate Advent Calendar for Jet-Setters: Artist Laila Gohar's Chocolate-Filled Creation Is Inspired by 24 Luxury Destinations
articles.summary: Egyptian artist Laila Gohar is putting her characteristically whimsical spin on a holiday tradition this year, teaming up with The Luxury Collection on a limited-edition advent calendar that takes its design and culinary cues from 24 destinations around the world. The $218 calendar, available through The Luxury Collection Boutique in the U.S. and Gohar World […]
articles.content:
Egyptian artist Laila Gohar is putting her characteristically whimsical spin on a holiday tradition this year, teaming up with The Luxury Collection on a limited-edition advent calendar that takes its design and culinary cues from 24 destinations around the world.

The $218 calendar, available through The Luxury Collection Boutique in the U.S. and Gohar World in select international markets, brings together the talents of illustrator Joana Avillez and Mexican chocolatier Casa Bosques. Designed to resemble the elaborate façade of a grand hotel, the collectible features 24 numbered drawers, each housing a custom chocolate inspired by one of the hotel group's properties. Related Stories How Netflix and the NFL Hope to Establish New Thanksgiving Eve Tradition With Game and U2 Half-Time Show: ‘We Want to Create Those Global Water Cooler Moments’ ‘Virgin River’ Renewed for Season 9 to Become Netflix’s Longest-Running Original Scripted Series

Casa Bosques founder Rafael Prieto worked with culinary teams across The Luxury Collection's portfolio to develop the 24 distinct flavors, which include saffron inspired by Dubai, black sesame by Kyoto, toasted coconut by South Caicos and banana and sea salt by Waikiki. Other destinations are represented by hazelnut praline (Paris) and smoked mesquite (Los Cabos).

“I love the anticipation of opening an advent calendar, especially during the holidays,” Gohar said in a statement. “Each drawer is a small world of its own, inspired by the flavors, traditions, and details that make destinations so special at this time of year. I hope each discovery sparks curiosity and joy.”

The artist, whose eponymous homewares label Gohar World specializes in surrealist interpretations of traditional tabletop objects, has made a name for herself turning food into elaborate, often fantastical installations.

As part of the collaboration, Gohar has also designed a series of holiday pop-ups modeled after old-world Parisian chocolate shops and Milanese apothecaries. The installations feature theatrical display windows and rows of drawers that echo the design of the calendar itself. At Paris' Prince de Galles hotel, artist and set designer Alix Bortoli created bespoke vitrines incorporating the raw ingredients used in the chocolates.

The pop-ups will run throughout the holiday season at Prince de Galles in Paris, The Joseph in Nashville, Solaz in Los Cabos and The Laurus in Singapore. Select properties will also host culinary and design programming tied to the collaboration.

The partnership is part of The Luxury Collection's ongoing World in Season initiative, which highlights the culinary and cultural traditions across the Marriott-owned brand's portfolio of more than 135 hotels and resorts in 41 countries and territories.

The limited-edition Laila Gohar x The Luxury Collection advent calendar retails for $218 and is available to purchase online and at participating hotels.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday will be here in a matter of weeks, and now, Robert Downey Jr. may just have teased that the character MCU fans most want to see in the film is officially coming. Discussions about Wanda Maximoff's eventual return to the MCU have been ongoing since the moment she died in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . Although her return was far from confirmed, fans never lost hope, and finally, in the post-credits scene of VisionQuest , she was confirmed to be alive once again in the franchise, with Doctor Doom coming to "collect" her in the same way that he had with Bruce Banner in one of the bonus scenes in Avengers: Endgame Encore .

Specifically, Doom told Scarlet Witch that her power would be his, signaling that she would be playing a role in Doomsday , considering that is when he will first be taking on the Avengers. However, that wasn't certain; it remained possible that we wouldn't see the Scarlet Witch's return on the big screen until Avengers: Secret Wars . Now, though, following a hilarious Instagram post from Robert Downey Jr. himself, it seems Wanda will be appearing alongside Doom in Doomsday . Check out Downey's post and more about what this might mean below.

Downey took to Instagram this morning with a hilarious image in which Doom is trying to set up a seating chart for Thanksgiving. While this could be passed off as being all in good fun, and it is certainly funny, it seems likely that there is more too this. And, what makes that particularly exciting is not only the fact that Wanda's name is included but also her location on the chart right next to Doctor Doom. Particularly given that Sue Storm is also seated next to Doom, this suggests that Wanda will be crucial in the story—and that is exactly what Wanda fans are going to want to hear.

View this post on Instagram There are some other notable inclusions on this image as well. For example, behind Doom's finger, it looks like the name "Peter" is being obscured. This could mean that Doctor Doom has Peter Parker/Spider-Man as well, supporting a theory following the post-credits scene of Spider-Man: Brand New Day , in which Spider-Man is shown as being in space. Additionally, names like Loki and Bruce are included, the former of which may confirm that Loki and Doom will be directly facing off against one another (which would be thrilling) and the other reinforcing that Bruce/Hulk is going to be a key part of Doom's plan, which comes as no surprise, given his raw power.

If anything, this image just serves to make excitement for Doomsday even higher, which is yet another major boost for the film following on the heels of the final trailer being released earlier this week and a brand-new teaser appearing yesterday.

Over the past year, Switch 2 owners have loudly made it known that they want Nintendo to release new content, whether it be paid or free, for Mario Kart World . And while Nintendo has released some new additions to the game in the wake of these requests, none of these content drops have been very substantial. Now, Nintendo is trying to rectify this just a bit with today's new update, but it still might not satisfy some fans.

Downloadable now, update version 1.9.0 for Mario Kart World most notably brings eight new tracks to the game. While this is somewhat of a major deal for MKW , it's worth noting that none of these courses are wholly original. Instead, they're merely remixed versions of tracks that have already been in the game. So a course like "Koopa Troopa Beach" now simply has a new iteration called "Koopa Troopa Beach 2" that players can experience, and so on. As a result, Nintendo still has yet to add any wholly new tracks to Mario Kart World , which will undoubtedly continue to prompt requests from players.

Outside of these new tracks, this Mario Kart World update does a handful of other things. Along with squashing a handful of bugs players have been discovering, this patch also introduces two new paths for Knockout Tour. articles.content:
Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix , have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for new season launches on broadcast — and beyond.

The breakthrough came four years prior when the success of AMC's Breaking Bad on Netflix helped the series avoid cancellation and become an award-winning hit for the cable network, prompting creator Vince Gilligan to give the streamer credit for keeping Breaking Bad on the air following the first of two Outstanding Drama Series Emmy wins in 2013.

Soon, there was a name for that — "the Riverdale phenomenon" — after the 2017 CW series which delivered OK, not spectacular ratings during its first season on the network before exploding on Netflix over the summer, leading to a ratings surge for the following season on the CW that fall.

"After that, everyone was like, 'Oh, I want my show on Netflix because then everyone will watch it,'" one industry veteran recalled.

Still, Netflix's output with the CW that Riverdale was part of notwithstanding, major library streaming pacts for on-air broadcast/basic cable series made after their first season were not that common, with NBC's The Blacklist and Blindspot , Fox's New Girl , Gotham and Lucifer and TNT's Animal Kingdom as notable examples, all selling in competitive situations. NBC's Good Girls was another streaming success story on Netflix. Licensed under an old co-production model Netflix employed in the late 2010s, its first season made its debut on Netflix in the U.S. on Jan. 1, 2019, just two months before the Season 2 launch on NBC. The series' success on Netflix and the generous fees coming from the streamer helped keep Good Girls on the air for four seasons despite declining linear ratings.

While lucrative for the studios, such third-party licensing agreements largely dried up when legacy media companies started launching their own streamers in 2019-20 and initially kept virtually of their series in a walled garden. That has gradually changed, with Netflix carrying more current ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox series than ever. (While Netflix has been dominating the field, there are rare exceptions with other third-party streamers, like CBS' Ghosts being available on Prime Video.)

What has evolved from the early-days exclusive SVOD pacts is that third-party deals now are largely not exclusive: the broadcast series are available on their sibling streamers which have both in-season (next day) and out-of-season (previous seasons) rights, while Netflix and other third-party streamers get the shows out-of-season, launching a season after it has finished its broadcast run.

That is in line with how syndication worked, though the streamer is getting new broadcast series much faster than the traditional model where shows had to make it to four seasons and 100 episodes to launch in syndication, first on local broadcast stations and then on cable.

"Then cable and local markets collapsed on top of each other, and eventually streaming essentially took the place of this syndication window. But not after four years, after one year," one industry veteran said.

Network series are now commonly sold to third-party platforms after their first season for an SVOD window that has two main entry points: a season dropping on the streamer 30 days after the season finale had been released, which shows such as Grey's Anatomy and the the CW's Sullivan's Crossing adhere to on Netflix, or at the start of the next broadcast season.

The latter was the case with New Girl and The Blacklist and is currently in play with NBC comedies Happy's Place and St. Denis Medical as well as Fox drama Doc , all on Netflix. In many cases, the fall entry point has evolved into a streaming season launch 30 or so days prior to the start of the next season on broadcast, providing an opportunity for people to get back into a show by catching up and reengaging.

That makes for strategic deployments like this fall's Netflix premieres of ABC's Will Trent and Shifting Gears timed to the next seasons' debut on broadcast with a strong promotional purpose. ( Will Trent dropped on Netflix two months ahead of the series' return on ABC, for Shifting Gears , the lead-in is about 30 days.)

Fox's Best Medicine and Animal Control — both owned by the network — also launch their previous season on Netflix a month ahead of the new seasons debuting on Fox.

Meanwhile, CBS' Fire Country is adding a wrinkle by going back an extra season. Its first season released on Netflix about two months ahead of its Season 3 premiere on CBS in 2024, and Season 2 made its Netflix debut about two months ahead of Season 4 debut on CBS in 2025. Interestingly, Fire Country 's presence on Netflix has been limited to these two seasons, with newer seasons only available on CBS sibling Paramount+. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

One of the earliest examples of such use of Netflix after the broadcast networks already had streamers in the corporate family was a one-year non-exclusive licensing deal CBS Studios made in September 2020 to put the first seasons of drama Evil and comedy The Unicorn on Netflix ahead of the premiere of their second seasons on CBS.

The stunt didn't help the Walton Goggins comedy, which was canceled by after two seasons. (The same happened to NBC's The Hunting Party despite a strong Season 1 launch on Netflix a little over a month into The Hunting Party 's second season on NBC.)

Meanwhile, Evil 's strong sampling on Netflix helped inform the decision to move the supernatural drama from CBS to Paramount+. The series' streaming performance also likely factored into the initial one-year non-exclusive licensing deal with Netflix getting extended to five years and the show's first three seasons.

The way streaming launches are plotted by series' owners is in line with the function basic cable served in its heyday for shows sold in off-network syndication whose latest season would become available on cable in September, just before the next season starts airing on broadcast.

To further promote a series' return on broadcast, shows used to do marathons on cable. What is a TV marathon's equivalent in the streaming era? Binging — or dropping the entire previous season on a platform like Netflix ahead of the new one's network premiere.

Exposure is great but it doesn't pay the bills — at least not directly — so the proliferation of Netflix licensing deals has been fueled by other motives too as networks and studios grapple with declines in linear ratings and the ad revenue attached to them.

"There is enhanced promotion, but also economics are driving these things," one industry insider said. "Studios are carrying deficits on these shows, they need to find revenue, so because because the four-year syndication window really is not there anymore, they have to find revenue."

For studios, the latter sometimes takes precedent. "From our standpoint, we're going to look at the money first, and then the marketing aspect second," one studio executive said.

The decisions are made with many factors in mind, including profit participants who get a portion of off-network revenue.

Talent agents who represent creatives have been lamenting the demise of the off-network syndication model, claiming that the money from streaming deals doesn't come close to the syndication windfall in covering shows' deficits and paying profit participants, with proceeds also down from the early days of the streaming wars when Netflix was paying premium for (predominantly exclusive) SVOD rights.

Studio executives argue that money is still there for the taking, but instead of one syndication revenue stream, there are multiple steaming ones as the era of large audiences watching network shows in syndication five days a week is gone. Now viewership is fractured, and so are streaming deals, non-exclusive over a myriad of platforms.

"Our business is not just streaming to the big ones, Netflix and Amazon; it's also AVOD, it's Roku and Tubi. There's multiple ways you can now make money, which is great," one TV executive said. "In the aggregate for individual shows probably will rarely get close to what a show could have made in its peak syndication days, so agents probably see that more than we do because they're focusing on the individual performance of one show in its U.S. life cycle." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Exactly six years after the Riverdale phenomenon, in the summer of 2023, we had the Suits phenomenon when an old USA Network series became the biggest show in America, breaking a slew of streaming ratings records and amassing eye-popping 57.7 billion minutes watched for the year despite only launching on Netflix U.S. in June.

It showed that cable series, once thought to be of no off-network syndication value, can draw big numbers when exposed to a new, wide audience on streaming.

That carried over to pay cable too, with Starz's biggest series, Outlander and Power, and Showtime's signature shows Dexter, Homeland, Shameless and Yellowjackets finding their way to Netflix, many of the deals driven by the series' producing studios.

With the dire state of the linear TV business, for basic cable networks that want to stay in the original scripted programming — and some pay cable ones too — a syndication-type deal with a major streamer is a do-or-die, a crucial revenue stream that allows them to afford scripted series.

That explains the big new $500 million licensing deal AMC recently made with Netflix for the entire The Walking Dead universe. Ever since Breaking Bad 's Netflix breakthrough, AMC has been licensing its biggest originals to the streamer, including The Walking Dead mothership for almost 15 years and Anne Rice's Immortal Universe, the newer ones shared with its own platform AMC+.

Meanwhile, Disney's FX is essentially a streaming brand on Hulu, delivering some of the platform's biggest hits, like American Horror Story, Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette, Shōgun , and The Bear .

In January, Netflix announced a deal with Paramount for 20 series, which, surprisingly, included a Taylor Sheridan Paramount+ original, Mayor of Kingstown .

HBO had previously licensed some of its originals to Netflix years after they had ended their run, including Sex and the City, Band of Brothers and Six Feet Under, with marquee series such as The Sopranos and Game of Thrones off limits. In contrast, Mayor of Kingstown is a current original on a rival streamer, part of Paramount+'s treasured Taylorverse. The other titles in the package are largely former CBS series, along with Matlock , licensed to Netflix only internationally.

I hear Mayor of Kingstown was a late addition as Netflix was not willing to take the other titles without it. I hear the Mayor of Kingstown producers leveraged the series' inclusion to get an extra season as Paramount+ had planned to end the show after Season 4. A renewal for an abbreviated fifth and final season was announced just days before the Netflix licensing deal, which includes the first four seasons of Mayor of Kingstown , was unveiled.

In May, David Ellison, then-CEO of Paramount, now co-CEO of Skydance, told Wall Street analysts that the company will continue to license select programming to third parties “for the foreseeable future.”

Amazon similarly made a Netflix deal for the first three seasons of MGM+'s acclaimed but not widely known sci-fi horror drama From, which has released four seasons and has been renewed for a fifth and final season. It has turned into a Suits/Riverdale -style phenomenon, amassing more than 5 billion minutes viewed in the U.S. in its first three weeks. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

As part of its Netflix licensing deal, Disney took a step further by lending a top Disney+ original series in its prime, Percy Jackson and the Olympians , for an unprecedented short, three-month window, along with the Ice Age movie franchise. The stunt is timed to the release of the new season of Percy Jackson on Disney+ on Nov. 20 and the new Ice Age movie, Boiling Point, on Feb. 5, 2027.

Touting the mutual benefits of the deal for Disney and Netflix, the latter's co-CEO Ted Sarandos joked about plugging rival Disney's Ice Age: Boiling Point on the streamer's earnings call last month, name-checking his Disney counterpart Josh D'Amaro by quipping, "You're welcome, Josh."

"We expect to have opportunities throughout for the best series and the best films with all the suppliers," Sarandos said about the Netflix licensing strategy. "It's a little complicated because all of our suppliers are also our competitors. Our deals bring in much needed revenue. They certainly build awareness, and the benefit of that awareness transfers back to them because it helps grow the value of their IP. So these deals really are win-win."

articles.title: 5 PlayStation Black Friday Deals You Won't Want to Miss Before November 2026 Ends
articles.summary: Courtesy of Sony With Black Friday approaching, PlayStation players will want to take advantage of several deals on some big games, including a few exclusives that are finally being marked at lower prices. From celebrated titles getting a sequel soon to some familiar hits of the past year, there are many different deals to choose from, offering dozens […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With Black Friday approaching, PlayStation players will want to take advantage of several deals on some big games, including a few exclusives that are finally being marked at lower prices. From celebrated titles getting a sequel soon to some familiar hits of the past year, there are many different deals to choose from, offering dozens to hundreds of hours of gameplay within certain titles. That being said, the Black Friday 2026 deals for PlayStation only last until November 30, so you'll want to grab whatever games you can quickly before they expire.

Some games in the Black Friday deals for PlayStation include some titles that are only dropping slightly in price, but that may be just enough for some players to purchase them. Games like Control Resonant and Baldur's Gate 3 are only knocking off a few dollars from their standard price, while other games like Resident Evil Requiem have made their Deluxe edition cost as much as the base version of the title. While not the greatest deals PlayStation is offering for the holiday season, they are still worth mentioning, as many players did not expect games of those caliber to be put on sale at all.

One of the most recent exclusives for the PlayStation 5 is Marvel's Wolverine , the Insomniac superhero title that features the six-clawed mutant from many X-Men stories. This action-adventure game is set within its own universe, telling a unique story with various X-Men characters and featuring hack-and-slash gameplay for players to get lost in. While this game hasn't been the recipient of as many accolades as Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man series, Marvel's Wolverine is still a gorgeous looking game with satisfying combat.

Currently, PlayStation has Marvel's Wolverine 's Standard Edition on sale for $49.69, marking around a 30% price decrease from its typical $69.99 cost. The game is a single-player adventure, meaning that it doesn't have as much play time as other titles, but multiple difficulty modes and combat challenges does add replayability to the game. The intense, gritty, M-rated combat of Marvel's Wolverine is very different compared to Marvel's Spider-Man , giving players more lethal action to sink their teeth into. For that reason, this can be a great title to pick up on Black Friday, but it isn't the only game on sale to feature Wolverine.

With the announcement of Robert Pattinson playing the next iteration of James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's upcoming 007 movie, perhaps players will be interested in trying 007 First Light . This game was developed by IO Interactive, the creators behind the modern Hitman series, with gameplay heavily reflecting the espionage and infiltration mechanics of that franchise. However, part of the charm of 007 First Light comes from a charming, excellent performance of James Bond by actor Patrick Gibson, whose depiction of the iconic spy has earned him a 2026 Game Award nomination.

Black Friday deals have marked down 007 First Light 50% of its original price, knocking it from $69.99 to $34.99. This is one of the best reviewed games of the year, featuring a unique story about Bond in his early years of becoming a legendary MI6 spy. Clever level design creates large sandboxes for players to tackle goals in whatever way they please, providing non-linear segments that reward ingenuity. Much like the adaptability of James Bond himself, players have to find ways to improvise and adjust plans to different situations, completing missions through suave cunning rather than brute force.

The little details of 007 First Light are what make it such an excellent Bond experience, from James' one-liner dialogue whenever he's caught somewhere he shouldn't be to the flashing "License to Kill" marker on screen when players are authorized to get violent. Solid gunplay mixes with classic Q gadgets to make this feel like the closest game to a James Bond movie since 007 GoldenEye , a landmark game. With various difficulty modes to increase replayability too, this Black Friday deal holds incredible value to fans of the 007 franchise.

Madden NFL 27 is listed on sale for $34.99, marking it down 50% from the Standard Edition's normal price of $69.99. The latest iteration of the football simulation Madden series, this title is perhaps the most visually impressive of the franchise yet, with hyper-realistic gameplay and graphics mirroring the sport its based on closely. Dynamic physics combine with game-changing weather mechanics to create one of the more immersive Madden games to come out recently. In an era where GTA 6 is redefining what high-quality realism looks like in games, Madden 27 is a great title that reflects that direction.

Madden 27 isn't without its problems with monetization and live service features that have plagued sports games over the years, but it is marginally better than College Football 27 's situation. In fact, the large price drop for the Standard Edition of Madden 27 makes in-game purchases more manageable for players who want to build a dynamic team to use online, especially while hype surrounding the 2026-27 football season continues. With a new roster of players with changed stats from the previous year, grabbing Madden 27 before Super Bowl LXI (Super Bowl 61) might be the right move.

The first Halo game to ever come to PlayStation consoles is Halo: Campaign Evolved , a remake of the classic Combat Evolved released in 2001. Campaign Evolved makes a lot of changes to the original title, adding gameplay elements from modern Halo games like Halo Infinite into the remake, such as new weapons, sprinting, and other features. While this can be alienating to older fans, new PlayStation players might appreciate the changes, as they relate to other shooters on Sony systems better, therefore allowing them to jump into Campaign Evolved with fewer obstacles.

Halo: Campaign Evolved is currently listed for $29.99 instead of $49.99, taking the game down 40% for PlayStation players. This title not only recreates all of the main story levels of Combat Evolved with new cutscenes and higher visual fidelity, but also adds three new prequel missions never seen in the classic sci-fi FPS before. In addition, free updates for the game plan to expand its multiplayer, adding classic modes like the PvE Firefight for many players to jump into together. With other never-before-seen features like a third-person POV, Halo: Campaign Evolved is a solid introduction to the series, despite lacking the franchise's competitive online PvP multiplayer.

The other big Marvel game sale going on for Black Friday is for Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls , the 4v4 fighting game made by Arc System Works, the developers behind other great games like Dragon Ball FighterZ and Guilty Gear Strive . This game is being listed at $39.59 for its base edition, taking it down 34% of its base price for players to pick it up before December 1, 2026. This game is one of the most complete fighting game releases of the year, having a strong 20 character roster comprised of different teams of characters, including:

Players can take control any of these characters in teams of four, with each fighter having incredibly deep move lists that reflect their unique powers and skill sets from Marvel Comics. The game features a robust story mode focused on any of the above teams as they try to face off against The Champion, a powerful cosmic entity looking for the universe's strongest fighters. Written by actual comic writers, the surprisingly deep story content in this game is on par with other fighting games like Mortal Kombat , which are known for weaving interesting narratives into their single-player experiences.

That being said, the online matchmaking of this title is solid too, giving players chances to join lobbies and participate in casual or ranked matches with their teams. Other modes like Survival offer roguelike challenges to unlock character outfits, giving players ways to play for various rewards besides the daunting task of facing others online. Although this PlayStation sale doesn't give players new DLC characters like Phoenix Cyclops, it does represent a great introduction to one of the best fighting games of the year for Black Friday.

articles.content:
Netflix is the only major industry player not currently funding the UK's anonymous whistleblowing service for complaints about bullying and harassment, it has been revealed.

The Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority ( CIISA ) has released its long-expected list of funders and the streamer's absence is notable, along with a number of talent agencies.

Last year, a Deadline analysis found that Channel 4, Disney and Amazon were among those refusing to pay annual CIISA fees, while at the time Netflix and Skydance (then Paramount) declined to confirm if they were providing support. UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy , a vocal backer of CIISA, has also previously chided MasterChef producer Banijay for the same thing. Today's register shows Channel 4, Disney, Amazon, Skydance and Banijay are now all paying, along with other production groups and major broadcasters plus Sky. The doc's producer, 72 Films, is funding CIISA. Its premiere preceded the allegations of sexually exploitative behavior against David Walliams — allegations that Walliams vehemently denies — placing bad behavior in UK entertainment in the spotlight.

UK agencies like Curtis Brown, Casarotto Ramsay & Associates, United Agents and YMU are not on the CIISA list. YMU repped Walliams until the start of this year.
